content.comment_body: Hello, I downloaded an existing [product_name] program. The program included four UDF function blocks that were marked with a question mark. After reading the manual about creating, editing, and importing UDFs, I tried those methods to make the indicator change to green. Here's what I did: I edited the UDF function block, saved it with the same identifier, imported it into my local library, and attempted to update it. I also removed the old UDF to replace it, but the software doesn't allow usage of the block. The manual states: [product_name] software shows a question mark if the UDF isn't available in the current library. To fix this, the UDF must be re-imported to the library. Anyone have any advice?
You need to save UDF files in a designated folder of your choice. Then, go into the software options under Tools > Options > UDF and select this folder for your UDFs.
Hi, Please check if the folder path for the UDF file contains non-unicode characters. This could prevent [product_name] from implementing the UDF correctly. Hope this helps.

When creating a UDF, you can save the file anywhere on your computer. Open your project, go to Tools > Options > UDF, then select ADD UDF. This will open your computer directory; navigate to where you saved the UDF and select it. Be aware that the UDF file must remain in the selected location for the program to use it. If you move the file, you must re-add it in your project before you can use it.

Thank you all for your suggestions. I tried renaming and placing the UDF file in the same folder I used for the [product_name] UDF library. In the end, the solution was to overwrite the existing UDF in the program, replacing it with a new one with a different identifier. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello everyone. How do you resolve the issue where, after creating a program with linked UDF files, there are no problems saving on the laptop, but errors occur during backup to a hard disk? Thanks in advance.
Please describe in more detail what errors you encounter when saving to the hard disk.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter issues with missing or incorrectly referenced UDF (User Defined Function) blocks in [product_name] software, indicated by question marks when opening programs. The primary challenge lies in unclear instructions for properly importing, referencing, and managing UDFs, particularly when files are moved, renamed, backed up, or restored. This causes broken links and prevents use of the desired function blocks. Even after consulting documentation and following various suggestions, users find error recovery, folder selection, and block replacement procedures ambiguous.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward and dependable process for re-importing, updating, or repairing missing UDF blocks to ensure they're recognized and usable within their program. They seek clear guidance on managing UDF files—especially concerning file locations and references.
